`getBoundingClientRect()` reports the element’s top-left corner relative to the viewport. For `root>plain>pin`, Chromium reports `x=10px` and `y=10px`, meaning its top-left corner is drawn at those coordinates in CSS pixels. Since `root>plain` is `position: static` (not positioned), there’s no additional offset from a positioned ancestor; the viewport-relative rectangle already captures the final on-screen position.
